group.passage:
Have your friends ever told you that “You are too sensitive!” or “ You shouldn’t think so much!” If so, you might be a highly sensitive person, or called HSP. [[1]]
What are the traits shared among most HSPs? First, they tend to avoid violent movies, which make them feel troubled and overwhelmed because they easily sympathize with those beaten. On the other hand, the beauty in nature, art, or kindness may easily move them to tears. [[2]] Spending time meditating makes them feel much more invigorated than shopping.
[[3]] An introvert prefers to accomplish tasks alone because they feel energy drained around large groups of people. However, an HSP craves novel experiences by joining new activities or discovering new places, and they tend to process or see things more profoundly than introverts, which also makes them more easily burned out psychologically. Around 30 % of HSPs are actually extroverts who crave interaction with people but also dread overstimulation.
Despite the recurring inconveniences in daily lives, HSPs have an edge over others. Because of greater sensitivity, they tend to have a gift for creating music or art works to let out the roaring waves in their hearts. They are often better listeners for friends in need than others.
[[4]] “Life gives you lemons because life knows you can make something sweet out of it.” Making the best of the sensitivity endowed is the answer to repel all the self-doubt.

options_bank.A: HSP may sometimes be mistaken for introverts, but, even for all the similarities, they actually have distinct personalities.
options_bank.B: First put forth by Dr. Elaine N. Aron in the mid 1990s, HSPs are actually quite common—around one in five people exhibits this trait.
options_bank.C: Being an HSP makes one more perceptive but also at times overwhelmed.
options_bank.D: Also, they tend to lead rich spiritual lives.
